messages:
Jordan Park: FYI VeloxPay reporting steady 429s this morning during payroll window, started ~08:03 UTC. customer says ~180 RPM but seeing bursts of 900 RPM for ~10s windows.
María Alvarez: Can you paste the client side pattern? is this a single process or many lambdas?
Jordan Park: They run 50 concurrent AWS Lambda invocations fan-out per payroll line item. Each lambda opens short-lived HTTP/1.1 connections and retries immediately on 429.
Sam O'Neill: immediate retries + high parallelism explains spike. Sounds like client-side throttling + no jitter. Do we have X-RateLimit headers from their requests?
Jordan Park: They sent a few request traces. Header example: 
```
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-limit: 300
x-rate-limit-reset: 15
x-request-id: rq_01F8K...
```
(They also included our 429 body: `{"error":"Rate limit exceeded"}`)
María Alvarez: Their reported 180 RPM steady with short 900 RPM bursts maps to a token-bucket refill mismatch. Lambdas likely align on minute boundaries causing minute-folding.
Sam O'Neill: Short checklist: 1) confirm per-API-key RPM/TPM limits for their account 2) ask for client rate pattern (histogram) 3) repro locally with same concurrency and backoff behavior.
Jordan Park: Asked them for histogram. They uploaded CloudWatch -> shows spikes when payroll batch starts: ~50 concurrent starts each doing ~20 requests quickly.
Sam O'Neill: Quick repro command to validate behavior (run from a single box):
```
# simple parallel requester (adjust concurrency/pause)
for i in `seq 1 50`; do 
  (for j in `seq 1 20`; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"input":"x"}' & done; wait) &
done; wait
```
This will create the same burst profile.
María Alvarez: Mitigations to recommend to customer: 1) add exponential backoff + jitter on 429s 2) reuse connections (keepalive / connection pooling) 3) stagger Lambda start times with small random jitter 4) reduce per-instance concurrency (eg from 50->10) 5) consider Dedicated pool or quota bump for predictable payroll window 6) enable client-side batching where possible.
Jordan Park: Sent those suggestions. They asked whether we can temporarily raise RPM for the 10-minute payroll window.
Sam O'Neill: We can offer a short-term rate bump if they commit to smoothing afterwards. Need to check their contract/tier. Ask CS for account plan and billing owner.
ops-bot: Auto: playbook reference -> https://redwood.ai/docs/support/playbooks/rpm-tpm-triage :point_right: use the "Burst mitigation" section.
support-bot: Note: collected sample request-id rq_01F8K... from customer. Logging shows 429 hits across edge-proxy for region eu-west-1 at 08:03:12 - 08:03:26 UTC.
María Alvarez: Next engineering asks: (a) can they share an anonymized request sample and SDK version? (b) enable debug logs for short window so we can correlate request-id -> backend node.
Jordan Park: Customer provided SDK v1.2.3 and agreed to add jitter. They also accepted a brief quota bump for the payroll run; I flagged billing.
Sam O'Neill: Final recommended reply to customer: include repro command, checklist to smooth fanout, offer support for a one-time quota increase, and ask them to run the repro and upload histogram. Keep responses short and include concrete numbers (target <= 300 RPM sustained, bursts < 450 RPM).
Jordan Park: I'll send that now and cc billing. Thanks all :thumbsup:
María Alvarez: Thanks — follow up if they still hit 429s after jitter/stagger.
